status: Pre-registered before any measured run (only the 4-run wiring smoke below ran). The rule is fixed; a new attempt is a new version and the FAIL stays. A PASS is necessary, not sufficient: the default changes only after the native client compatibility gate (G-kompat, the user's manual test).
question: Does dropping Connection: close from 206 stream responses (STREAM_KEEP_ALIVE=true) shorten the time to first byte of repeated bounded Range requests for an HTTP/1.1 client over TLS at 20 and 80 ms RTT, without a regression at 1 ms RTT or for an HTTP/2 client?

findings_before_registration.upstream_274: Upstream 92fcb8d (#274, 'Kapcsolat zárása stream befejezésekor', 2026-09-06) adds only the header; the PR has no description, the commit no body, and no related issue was found. No documented rationale; the invariants it could protect are tested instead (below).
findings_before_registration.http2: The app always serves HTTPS (settings/service.py play URLs), and Hypercorn negotiates h2 via ALPN. The h2 library strips connection-specific headers (normalize_outbound_headers), so HTTP/2 clients already keep one connection; only HTTP/1.1 clients pay a TCP+TLS handshake per Range request.
findings_before_registration.short_body: Hypercorn 0.18 / h11 0.16: a response body shorter than its Content-Length (relay failure after the headers) leaves the server in ERROR and closes the connection at once; covered by server/tests/test_stream_keep_alive.py under a real Hypercorn.
findings_before_registration.behind_a_proxy: Behind a reverse proxy the client-facing connection is the proxy's; the header only affects the proxy-to-app hop.

source.manifest_method: sha256 over 'path:git-blob-id' lines of git ls-tree -r HEAD server/app (as gsp02-v4)
source.candidate_contents: feature/stream-performance @ ecab461 + 098838e (config.stream_keep_alive, default False = today's Connection: close) + 69b899a (harness only).
source.note: server/app at the registration commit equals the image source (checked).

harness.what_is_real: the product image and its normal start, TLS (self-signed, ALPN h2/http1.1), API-key auth, playback limit, relay and libtorrent, the real stream endpoint with Range, Hypercorn's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling.
harness.what_is_synthetic: the swarm (8 local seeders + local tracker on an --internal Docker network), the fixture rows and signed tokens (sp_app_fixture.py --playbacks 2), the remote-viewer RTT (H3 latency_proxy.py), the client (httpx 0.28.1, a connection pool per client).

C0.role: baseline: image default, Connection: close on every stream response

CK.role: candidate: no Connection header on 206 responses

scenario.warm_torrent: per run, playback token 0 reads the whole 256 MiB file (Range bytes=0-) with its own client before the series, so every piece is local; not a sample.
scenario.series: after 2 s settle, a fresh client (empty pool) and playback token 1 send 20 sequential bounded Range GETs of 1 MiB, 200 ms apart, read to the end: request 1 at 0, request 2 the tail probe, then 18 golden-ratio spread offsets (the same in every run). Request 1 always opens a new connection; in C0 every request does, in CK the HTTP/1.1 client reuses it.
scenario.cells: rtt1, rtt20, rtt80: HTTP/1.1 client through the H3 proxy with 0.5/10/40 ms one-way delay; rtt80/h2: the same at 80 ms with --http2 (guard: no change expected).

expected_mechanism.http1: C0: every request pays the TCP handshake (1 RTT) and the TLS 1.3 handshake, whose client Finished carries the request (1 RTT to the first byte), about 2 RTT through the proxy; CK: request 1 the same, requests 2-20 about 1 RTT -> expected repeat gain about 1 RTT (about 1, 20 and 80 ms; the smoke shows 172 vs 88 ms at 80 ms RTT), plus a warm TCP window for the 1 MiB body (total_s, descriptive).
expected_mechanism.http2: both arms one connection (the header is stripped by h2): no difference expected.

wiring_smoke.note: Not a measurement: this image and harness, series [{C0, CK} x 1] in rtt80 and rtt80/h2, 4 runs; the checks below are asserted at registration.
wiring_smoke.checks: C0 HTTP/1.1: 20 connections, 20 Connection: close; CK HTTP/1.1: 1 connection, 0 Connection: close; h2: 1 connection in both arms; 0 non-206, 0 errors, 0 app tracebacks

decision_rule.primary_metric: series.repeat_ttfb_s_p50 (per-run median TTFB of requests 2..20, seconds)
decision_rule.pooling: both series pooled: n = 10 runs per arm and cell; failed runs excluded and counted
decision_rule.statistic: difference of means (CK - C0); 10 000 bootstrap resamples per test, seed 20261114; one-sided bootstrap p-values
decision_rule.improvement: primary metric in a key cell: H0 'difference >= 0' rejected by Holm over the 2 key cells
decision_rule.regression: any guard test (3 guard metrics in all 4 cells, 12 tests): H0 'difference <= 0' rejected by Holm over the 12 tests
pass_if_all: CK: non-206 = 0, client errors = 0 and extra connections = 0 (one connection per series, also in the h2 cell) in every non-failed run, none missing
failed runs and tracebacks with an application frame: CK <= C0
descriptive_only: series.repeat_ttfb_s_p95, ttfb_s_p50, headers_s_*, total_s per request
C0 connections and Connection: close counts (wiring, reported)
warm-up seconds, app CPU and memory
decision_rule.otherwise: FAIL: stream_keep_alive stays False and SP09 closes without change.
decision_rule.after_pass: STREAM_KEEP_ALIVE stays False until the native client compatibility gate (G-kompat: Stremio desktop, Android, Android TV, iOS, Kodi, VLC; the user's manual test on a local Docker build) passes; then the user decides the default.

infra_retry: The controller reruns a run once when it failed by Docker itself (docker run exit 125, 'error waiting for container', 'error during connect', 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon'); the record keeps the first failure as infra_retry.

runner.where: host shell in the SP09 worktree, local Docker Desktop, sequential with every other measurement (no build or other gate while it runs).
runner.runs_and_time: 2 series x 5 reps x 4 cells x 2 arms = 80 runs, about 1 min each -> about 1.5 h
